newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua plans $50 million coffee bonds issue.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua plans $50 million coffee bonds issue.

text.p: Nicaragua's coffee growers will issue $50 million in coffee bonds after the new government takes office on January 10, Nicaragua's top coffee grower said on Friday.

The bonds will help finance coffee production and overcome a lack of credit that has stifled coffee production in recent years, David Robleto, head of the Union of Nicaraguan Coffee Growers (Unicafe), told a news conference.

"For a rapid solution of the financing problem, we will issue $50 million in coffee bonds backed by the Nicaraguan government which will placed with foreign banks and sold by stock agencies," Robleto said.

He said the issue of the bonds was "almost certain" and would take place after right-wing President-elect Arnoldo Aleman, himself a coffee grower and former leader of the coffee growers' union, takes office in January.
He said the money from the bonds would go to coffee producers, not the government, which will likely not be able to help the coffee growers in the short term due to budget restrictions.
"This issue of (coffee) bonds has been done by Guatemala and Costa Rica, and in a different fashion in Honduras," he said.
He said the bonds would have five-year maturities and likely pay 10 percent per year.
Aleman has named Robleto as Minister of Foreign Cooperation, the ministry in charge of coordinating foreign aid and loans, in his future cabinet.
At the news conference, Robleto would not say who would replace him as head of Unicafe or if he would maintain the position despite his new job.
